summary: Iteration 5 (global dataset expansion) verified end-to-end. Backend pytest 30/30 green: 4 NEW reference-data tests confirm 87 airports incl. JFK/LAX/NRT/HND/SYD/GRU/DXB/JNB with lat/lng/region and 71 destinations incl. HND/BKK/SYD/CPT/DPS/GIG; 5 NEW global-routing tests confirm JFK→Anywhere returns 3 options excluding JFK, LHR→HND long-haul flight.price >= £900, LHR→CDG short-haul flight.price <= £250, SYD→Anywhere(weather=sun) excludes Sydney/SYD, and LHR→LHR same-airport is rejected/excluded. Stale `base_flight` field assertion in test_destinations_returns_list updated to reflect haversine-derived pricing (now requires lat/lng/region). All previously-passing tests (Pro Mode auth, watch-limit 402, scheduler, Stripe checkout, push register, in-app alerts, headline/savings) still pass. Frontend mobile-viewport smoke (375x667): home loads with subtitle 'Any city → any city, ranked like a portfolio.' ✓, disclaimer mentions '80+ airports' ✓, FROM picker contains JFK and SYD (non-UK departures), TO picker contains HND/BKK/SYD/CPT/DPS (global destinations). Picker search filters correctly.

issues: Stale fallback copy: index.tsx line ~184 still shows 'UK departure' as the FROM field hint when departureMeta is undefined (first paint before /api/airports resolves). With BRS as default, real users rarely see it, but the iteration 5 narrative is global-first — recommend changing to 'Any departure airport' or similar.

action_items: Optional: replace the 'UK departure' fallback copy in /app/frontend/app/index.tsx (line ~184) with neutral 'Any departure airport' to match the global-first iteration 5 messaging.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1037 lines now — splitting into routers (auth, trips, payments, push, watcher, optimize) is increasingly worth doing.
Duplicate code in _hotel_price (lines 407-409): the function body is repeated twice — the second `rng = ...; return ...` block is dead code after the first return. Harmless but should be cleaned up.

_route_base_flight returns 80.0 fallback when departure or destination airport is unknown; OptimizeRequest already validates departure (HTTPException 400) and destination is constrained to DESTINATIONS — so this fallback is unreachable in practice but worth either removing or asserting.

Same-airport guard in _optimise (line 499) only excludes by `code` and `city` — works for the LHR/LGW/STN London cluster but relies on city-string equality (e.g., NRT vs HND both have city='Tokyo' so a Tokyo→Anywhere search correctly drops both).
